chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A young boy was brought to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to supplicate for him, and he had 'qanazi' (partly shaven head), so he refused to supplicate for him and ordered that his head be shaved, and the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) ordered the shaving of the stomach hair.

key_terms.قَنَازِعُ: Plural of Qanaza, referring to a style of shaving part of the head while leaving other parts, often associated with pre-Islamic or specific cultural practices.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling or practice regarding 'Al-Qanaza'a' (partly shaven head) in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) declined to supplicate for a boy with 'qanazi'—a pre-Islamic or early Islamic grooming style where hair was shaved in patches—demonstrating that this specific aesthetic was abhorrent to him. He ordered the boy's head to be fully shaved, including the 'stomach' of the head (the central crown area), thereby establishing the removal of this partial shaving as a sign of returning to natural, clean grooming (fitrah) and rejecting vanity or tribal markers.
